clue.text: See 4
Coin that's fragrant

definitions.meaning: to coin money is to ... it, and a ... is where coins are struck
minty, smelling of the herb ..., as in a fresh fragrant scent

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the coin-making verb and the aromatic herb share the same four-letter word.

clue.text: Group's unlimited character to hack into?

indicators.note: into says the cutting word goes inside the trimmed word for character
unlimited strips the first and last letters off the word for character

parts.note: ethos means the characteristic spirit or character of a person or community
to hew is to hack or chop

explanation.surface: A band's leader of chaos is a character who cuts in on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group's' is the definition, the possessive standing for 'Group is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who are the famous British rock band, the theme of this puzzle.

clue.text: 3's normal fees I foolishly invested in sweets

definitions.note: a song by the band at 3-down

indicators.note: invested in means wrapped up inside, so the anagram is put inside the word for sweets

parts.note: ices are frozen sweets, ice creams

indicators.note: foolishly says these letters are put together in a silly new order

explanation.surface: Someone has foolishly sunk ordinary payments into confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' places the anagram after the first two letters of the sweets, so it sits wholly inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: I Can See for Miles is a 1967 hit single by The Who, the band at 3-down.

clue.text: More than one flower exists either way beneath upturned bush with no berry?

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath puts the second part below the first
upturned in a down clue turns the trimmed shrub's letters upside down, so they read backwards
with no says the fruit word is taken away from the shrub's name

parts.note: the cranberry is a low evergreen shrub
taken as written, removed from the shrub's name
exists means is

indicators.note: either way means the little word is given forwards and then backwards

parts.note: exists means is

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether a fruitless shrub flipped over still counts as several blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: CRANBERRY with no BERRY leaves CRAN, upturned to NARC; 'either way' gives IS and SI beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi is the plural of narcissus, the daffodil family of spring flowers.

clue.text: Useful flipping herb, pointless when trimmed round it

indicators.note: round says the trimmed word goes around the flipped herb
when trimmed says the word for pointless loses a letter at its front

parts.note: futile means pointless, achieving nothing

indicators.note: flipping turns the herb's name over so it reads backwards

parts.note: basil is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A cook mutters that the blasted herb is useless once it has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' poses as a mild British curse; 'round it' means the trimmed word goes round the flipped herb, 'it'. 'when trimmed' takes only the leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something utilisable can be put to use, so it is useful in the plain sense.

clue.text: See 17
Era primarily old, life without iron, not quite Neanderthal — was it?

definitions.text: Era primarily old, life without iron, not quite Neanderthal — was it?

indicators.note: primarily means take just the first letter of the word era
without says the chemical symbol for iron is removed from the word life

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: not quite drops the final letter of the word for a Neanderthal type

parts.note: a Neanderthal, in slang, is someone dim and thick

explanation.surface: A question whether the age of old stone tools, before metal, came just before Neanderthal man.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: an early stone-tool stage before metal, and before Neanderthals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eolithic describes the dawn of the Stone Age, the supposed earliest era of crude flint tools.

clue.text: County where soldier's on edge

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits just before the second, as in an across clue placing

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker of the fighting caste, so an ant is a soldier in crossword terms
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A place where a soldier stands on the brink.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six historic counties of Northern Ireland, an example of a county.

clue.text: Throw back first bits of trash into my old skip

indicators.note: throw back means the gathered letters are read in reverse order
first bits of takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Someone tosses rubbish back into their own old skip.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'trash into my old' are TIMO, thrown back. 'skip' is a British rubbish container in the surface but the verb 'leave out' as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to leave it out or pass over it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Loudly complain, rep plonked contents here?

indicators.note: loudly signals that the words are spoken out and the result is what is heard

parts.note: to whine is to complain; a seller is a sales rep

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a complaint because a sales rep dumped his things in the place.
explanation.walkthrough: WHINE SELLER said out loud gives the answer. 'Plonk' is British slang for cheap wine, so the store for plonk is where its 'contents' go.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar for wine is where bottles of plonk, cheap wine, are kept, a whimsical description.

clue.text: A sign about double parking in Middle Eastern city

indicators.note: about means the star sign goes around the two Ps

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: double means the abbreviation for parking is written twice

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An astrological sign concerns a car double-parked in a Levantine city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a major city in northern Syria, an ancient Middle Eastern settlement.

clue.text: Victim stabbed by the blinking thing earlier

indicators.note: stabbed by means the second piece is pushed into the first

parts.note: prey is a victim, one hunted or preyed upon
a cursor is the blinking marker on a computer screen

explanation.surface: A victim was knifed earlier by some blinking creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blinking' poses as a mild curse but describes the flashing cursor.
explanation.definitionFit: Precursory means coming before or preceding, so it is a formal synonym for earlier.

clue.text: Ideas set out in part of the metropolis

indicators.note: out means the letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: New concepts are laid out in a district of a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IDEAS SET, sent 'out', rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: New York's East Side is a well-known district of Manhattan, an example of a city area.

clue.text: Like base about which sort of gas rises

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of comparison

indicators.note: about which says the gas abbreviation goes around the word for base

parts.note: CS gas is a type of tear gas
end is a base or bottom

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on a base around which some gas is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks chemical but means bottom; 'which' refers back to it, so the gas sits about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise or climb, a straightforward synonym in the same tense.

clue.text: Described like the Three Blind Mice?

definitions.meaning: described in full and particular terms, minutely set out
in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off their tails

explanation.definitionFit: Detailed means fully described; split as de-tailed it means having had tails removed.

clue.text: 3's fix with dance champion

definitions.note: a song by the band at 3-down

parts.note: to pin is to fix or fasten
a ball is a formal dance
a wizard is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A fixed dance contest with a champion, in the theme band's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinball Wizard is The Who's 1969 single from the rock opera Tommy, by the band at 3-down.

clue.text: Caper and egg plant

parts.note: a lark is a prank or caper
to egg on is to spur

explanation.surface: Capers and eggs on a plate with some vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' and 'egg' pose as food, but 'egg' is the verb, as in egg on.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flowering plant, delphinium family, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: "Nasty" about right for "lovely"!

indicators.note: about means the word for nasty goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: scummy means nasty, foul

explanation.surface: Someone swaps the word nasty for lovely in the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: SCUMMY goes 'about' R. SCRUMMY is British slang for delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrummy is informal British for delicious, a lovely taste, so it means lovely.

clue.text: A stroke of genius: staff heard of sound!

indicators.note: heard signals that the words are spoken and the result is what reaches the ear

parts.note: a coup is a stroke of genius and a stick is a staff, so these give a coup stick

explanation.surface: A brilliant move: the staff were praised by ear.
explanation.walkthrough: A COUP STICK spoken aloud runs together as the answer, the P of coup being silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic means relating to sound or hearing, so 'of sound' is a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: Rotten cold before game

indicators.note: before puts the first piece in front of the second

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: A cold that strikes before a card game is rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for poor or rotten in quality, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Writer gets to attempt creative writing

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An author gets the chance to have a go at producing fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is imaginative literature in verse, a form of creative writing.

clue.text: Extraction of principled gentlemen's agreement

indicators.note: Extraction says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Drawing out a gentlemen's agreement among men of principle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise or undertaking, so it is a form of agreement.

clue.text: 3's alternative

definitions.meaning: a song by the band at 3-down, their 1966 single
an alternative is a replacement, one used instead

explanation.definitionFit: Substitute is a 1966 Who single and also means a replacement or alternative.

clue.text: Smack for party

definitions.meaning: a smack is a blow, a hit
a lively party or celebration, in slang

explanation.definitionFit: A bash is both a heavy blow and, informally, a big party.

clue.text: Second ago

definitions.meaning: to second is to support, as a motion in a meeting
in time past, as in ten years since

explanation.definitionFit: To back is to support or second; back also means in the past, as ago does.

clue.text: 3's fury about genders understandable, ultimately

definitions.note: a song by the band at 3-down

indicators.note: about means the word for fury wraps around the two letters

parts.note: ire is fury, anger
M and F are abbreviations for male and female, two genders

indicators.note: ultimately means take only the last letter of the word that precedes it

explanation.surface: Anger over gender questions is understandable in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: I'm Free is a song from The Who's rock opera Tommy, by the band at 3-down.

clue.text: 3's music, bag of tricks?

definitions.note: a song by the band at 3-down

indicators.note: tricks hints the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: The band's songs are a conjuror's bag of tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSIC and BAG are rearranged, the anagram signal being 'tricks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic Bus is a 1968 single by The Who, the band at 3-down.
